question: What is the main difference between a medical emergency and a surgical emergency?

options.A: Surgical emergencies never involve internal bleeding
options.B: Medical emergencies always require immediate surgery
options.C: Medical emergencies only happen outside the hospital
options.D: Surgical emergencies usually require an operation to fix

explanation: You've got this! Surgical emergencies involve physical trauma or acute organ trouble that typically needs an operation to fix, while medical emergencies usually stem from internal illnesses. Think surgery vs. medicine! [learn more](GNS221_U3_T1#GNS221_U3_T1_h1)

question: Why is the first sixty minutes after a major injury famously called the 'golden hour'?

options.A: Patients are most cooperative during this time
options.B: Surgeons only perform operations during this timeframe
options.C: Lab results take exactly one hour to return
options.D: Treatment during this window gives the highest chance of survival

explanation: Spot on! That first hour is precious. Getting prompt care during this window dramatically lowers the risk of death or lasting damage after a severe trauma. [learn more](GNS221_U3_T1#GNS221_U3_T1_h1)

question: What is the main goal of emergency triage in the hospital?

options.A: To collect payment information from patients
options.B: To complete a detailed family medical history
options.C: To assign a private room to every arriving patient
options.D: To sort patients based on the severity of their condition

explanation: Great thinking! Triage is simply sorting patients by how sick they are, making sure the most critical, life-threatening cases get seen first. [learn more](GNS221_U3_T1#GNS221_U3_T1_h2)

question: A patient rushes in with severe chest pain, while another has a minor finger cut. According to triage rules, what should you do first?

options.A: Ask both patients to sit in the waiting room together
options.B: Treat the chest pain patient immediately
options.C: Treat the finger cut patient because it will take less time
options.D: Register the finger cut patient first to clear the desk

explanation: You nailed it! Chest pain and trouble breathing point to a high-risk emergency. They always take top priority over minor cuts and scrapes. [learn more](GNS221_U3_T1#GNS221_U3_T1_h2)

question: In the ABCDE emergency assessment, what does the letter 'C' stand for?
explanation: Well done! In the ABCDE routine, C stands for Circulation. It's all about checking pulses, blood pressure, and stopping any heavy bleeding. [learn more](GNS221_U3_T1#GNS221_U3_T1_h3)

question: Why must a nurse check the airway before breathing and circulation during an emergency?

options.A: A blocked airway will cause death regardless of heart function
options.B: Doctors only look at the airway during emergencies
options.C: It is a hospital rule with no medical reason
options.D: Airway assessment takes the least amount of time

explanation: Makes total sense! If air can't get through, nothing else matters because the body gets zero oxygen. Clearing the airway is always step number one. [learn more](GNS221_U3_T1#GNS221_U3_T1_h3)

question: In the FAST mnemonic used to spot a stroke, what does the letter 'T' stand for?
explanation: You got it! T stands for Time—meaning it's time to call for emergency help right away if you notice any stroke signs. [learn more](GNS221_U3_T1#GNS221_U3_T1_h4)

question: A patient having a severe allergic reaction has wheezing, swollen lips, and crashing blood pressure. What medication is given first?
explanation: Brilliant! Epinephrine is a lifesaver in anaphylaxis because it quickly opens up the airways and brings blood pressure back up. [learn more](GNS221_U3_T1#GNS221_U3_T1_h4)

question: What do we mean by an 'acute abdomen' in clinical practice?

options.A: Chronic indigestion caused by spicy food
options.B: Sudden, severe abdominal pain that often requires urgent surgery
options.C: A normal feeling of fullness after a large meal
options.D: A mild muscle cramp after heavy exercise

explanation: Spot on! An 'acute abdomen' is a red flag for sudden, severe belly pain that usually means trouble inside, like appendicitis or a perforation, needing quick surgical eyes. [learn more](GNS221_U3_T1#GNS221_U3_T1_h5)

question: Why are doctors and nurses careful about giving strong pain relief right away to someone with undiagnosed, severe belly pain?

options.A: Analgesics always cure appendicitis without an operation
options.B: Patients with stomach pain cannot swallow pills
options.C: Pain medicines cause immediate kidney failure
options.D: It can mask important physical signs and delay necessary surgery

explanation: Good clinical thinking! Masking the pain can hide how the illness is progressing, making it tricky for surgeons to figure out what's really wrong inside. [learn more](GNS221_U3_T1#GNS221_U3_T1_h5)

question: Why is an unconscious patient who is still breathing placed in the recovery position?

options.A: To make it easier to start an intravenous line
options.B: To prevent the tongue from blocking the airway and allow drainage
options.C: To lower the patient's blood pressure safely
options.D: To prepare the patient for immediate surgery

explanation: You got it! This position keeps the airway safe by stopping the tongue from sliding back, and lets any saliva or vomit drain safely out of the mouth. [learn more](GNS221_U3_T1#GNS221_U3_T1_h6)

question: What is the best immediate action to control heavy bleeding from a wound on someone's arm?

options.A: Giving the patient large amounts of oral fluids
options.B: Elevating the arm above the level of the heart only
options.C: Applying direct pressure with a clean dressing
options.D: Pouring rubbing alcohol directly into the open cut

explanation: Awesome! Direct pressure is your best friend here. It squeezes the bleeding vessels against the bone so a clot can quickly form. [learn more](GNS221_U3_T1#GNS221_U3_T1_h6)

question: What does the SBAR acronym stand for during a patient handover?
explanation: Easy peasy! SBAR stands for Situation, Background, Assessment, and Recommendation. It keeps your shift handovers clear and professional. [learn more](GNS221_U3_T1#GNS221_U3_T1_h7)

question: Why is a structured handover so important when transferring an emergency patient to intensive care?

options.A: It replaces the need to write patient chart notes
options.B: It allows the receiving nurse to avoid reading past history
options.C: It prevents critical clinical details from being missed
options.D: It reduces the financial cost of hospital admission

explanation: You're spot on! Handovers are vital communication bridges. A structured format makes sure nothing important gets forgotten when passing care to a new team. [learn more](GNS221_U3_T1#GNS221_U3_T1_h7)
